cryptohome: fix IsAttestaionPrepared for tpm2 After CL:1418984, TpmIsAttestationPrepared in cryptohomed uses GetEnrollmentPreparations to get "is prepared" status in the "distributed" (TPM 2.0) case. Before this CL, it was just returning TRUE if there was at least one element in the returned enrollment_preparations map. That was wrong, since GetEnrollmentPreparations returns a map with true/false values for all known ACA types. So, even when the attestation is not prepared yet, the map is not empty, just all values are false. This CL fixes the logic and checks if there is at least one true value in the map instead. BUG=b:124085203 TEST=Run "cryptohome --action=tpm_attestation_status" on an unowned device with TPM2.0; check that "Attestation Prepared: false". Repeat after going through owning and preparing for attestation, check that "Attestation Prepared: true" this time. clock: define the function clock_enable_module to all EC chips The API clock_enable_module(MODULE_FAST_CPU, x) allows common layer code to set the CPU frequency to turbo or normal when it is needed. However, not all of the EC chips support/implement the function. It causes build error if this function is added to the common codes which most of EC chips will use (EX: vboot_hash.) This CL fixes this issue by defining the function as weak by default. This CL also implements the clock_enable_module function for NPCX7 chip. BRANCH=none BUG=b:77608104 TEST=pass "make buildall" TEST=on npcx7_evb/yorp, with follow-up CL, check that security computation becomes faster and the clock goes back to normal frequency after the computation finishes. chromeos-bootimage: use altfw payload hashing for all The primary purpose of this change is to add the hash for the diag payload. The only remaining payload that isn't hashed is seabios, so I added that for the sake of consistency (under the assumption that just because a hash is there it doesn't mean it has to be used, and seabios is now opt-in on master so it shouldn't slow down the common case). This change also changes the name of the hash file from altfw_hash/${name}.sha256 to altfw/${name}.sha256 to make it easier for the firmware to derive the hash file name from the image name (by merely appending .sha256). BUG=b:124358784 TEST=USE="tianocore seabios diag_payload" emerge-sarien depthcharge coreboot chromeos-bootimage cbfstool /build/sarien/firmware/image-sarien.bin print -r FW_MAIN_A | grep -i altfw altfw/tianocore.sha256 0x8840 raw 32 none altfw/seabios.sha256 0x88c0 raw 32 none altfw/diag.sha256 0x8940 raw 32 none Change-Id: I59f8e590fda8f453e00a80aa402808923761c7b5 Signed-off-by: Matt Delco <delco@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1470548 Tested-by: Matt Delco <delco@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org>
